newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police rule out guerrillas for shop fire.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police rule out guerrillas for shop fire.

text.p: A firebomb gutted a Belfast city centre clothes shop but Northern Ireland police said on Wednesday they did not believe guerrillas were behind the attack.
"Police have described the make-up of this device as crude and certainly do not link it with any paramilitary involvement," a Royal Ulster Constabulary spokesman said.

Earlier there were fears the fire could herald the start of an IRA guerrilla blitz. British security sources said they were probing whether the device was a type previously used by outlawed Irish Republican Army guerrillas.
The IRA, which is fighting to end British rule, has stepped up hostilities in the past month with a series of rocket and bomb attacks and a shooting, in which a policeman was wounded.
Pro-British Loyalist hardliners are suspected of launching retaliatory attacks on two Catholic civilians who are well-known republicans opposed to British sovereignty.

Before declaring a September 1994 truce, which collapsed last February, the IRA waged a bombing war against so-called "economic targets" in town centres, using explosives and small firebombs to lethal effect.
